claims.text: Standard AIMD thermodynamic integration is prohibitively expensive for Ta-based refractory high-entropy alloys.
Classical EAM potentials are inaccurate for Ta-based refractory high-entropy-alloy liquids.
Failures of TOR-TILD or similar approaches in multicomponent spaces often arise because classical potentials cannot represent the complex disordered liquid structure of refractory HEAs.
An MLP trained on AIMD liquid configurations of the target composition can accurately represent the complex interactions in the liquid state.
Including high-coordination environments and variations in short-range order in the training set improves coverage of local environments typical of refractory liquids.
Free-energy differences can be estimated by ensemble averaging the potential-energy difference between a reference state and the target MLP state.
Sampling a narrow ensemble of relevant liquid configurations avoids thermodynamic integration over the full phase space.
Restricting sampling to relevant liquid configurations reduces computational cost while maintaining free-energy accuracy.
The proposed MLP perturbation scheme will produce free-energy differences with less than 5% error relative to full thermodynamic integration.
The proposed scheme will reduce computational cost by a factor of 10 to 100.
The proposed method will resolve subtle free-energy differences between competing liquid structures in the Ta-based HEA.
The accuracy of the MLP depends on the quality and diversity of its training set.
Inadequate representation of the alloy's liquid structure in the training set can bias the free-energy estimates.
The perturbation scheme requires sufficient phase-space overlap between the reference and target states.
The perturbation calculation may fail if the reference state is too dissimilar from the target state.
The realized speedup depends on the MLP architecture and computational hardware.
The method may not transfer to solid-state free-energy calculations or to alloys with substantially different liquid structures.

contradictions.description: The prediction requires less than 5% free-energy error, but the experiment declares falsification only above 10%, leaving results from 5% through 10% inconsistent with the stated prediction without falsifying it.
The predicted speedup is 10–100×, whereas falsification occurs only below 5×, leaving a 5–10× result below the predicted range but not classified as falsifying.
